findings.title: Accidental submodule pointer committed
findings.body: A gitlink entry named `sentry-repo` is added, pointing to subproject commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a, which is the base commit of this PR. This appears to be an accidentally committed git submodule; it will make the repository depend on an external/self-referential submodule, break checkouts/CI for other contributors, and is unrelated to the feature. It should be removed from the PR.

findings.title: Cache key uses process-local hash()
findings.body: The cache key uses Python's built-in `hash()` on sorted project IDs. Tuple hashing is randomized per interpreter process unless PYTHONHASHSEED is fixed, so different web workers/processes generate different keys for the same logical project set. This defeats cross-process caching, and `invalidate_upsampling_cache()` at line 73 deletes a different key than the one workers wrote, so invalidation is ineffective. Use a stable serialization such as `",".join(map(str, sorted(project_ids)))` instead of `hash(tuple(...))`.

findings.title: Upsampling decision ignores the query actually being executed
findings.body: `_get_event_stats` receives a `query` argument, but `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(..., request)` determines whether the query is error-focused from `request.GET["query"]` only. This endpoint calls `_get_event_stats` with different query strings for dashboard discover split logic, such as `errors_only_query = f"({query}) AND !event.type:transaction"` and transaction-only queries. In those cases the actual query can be error-only or transaction-only while the decision is based on the original request query, so `count()` may be left untransformed for an errors-only split query or transformed for a transaction-only query, producing incorrect stats or Snuba errors. Pass the current `query` parameter into the helper and use it for the error-focus check.

findings.title: Substring check misclassifies negated/mixed queries
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` only checks whether `"event.type:error"` appears anywhere in the request query. A query like `!event.type:error` contains that substring but selects non-error/transaction events; similarly `event.type:transaction OR event.type:error` includes transactions. For the discover dataset this can enable `upsampled_count()` (`sum(sample_weight)`) on transaction rows where `sample_weight` is not available or meaningful, causing Snuba errors or wrong counts. Parse the actual event.type filter, including negation and OR, rather than doing a raw substring search.

findings.title: toInt64 truncates fractional sample weights
findings.body: The new `upsampled_count` aggregate wraps `sum(sample_weight)` in `toInt64`. Sample weights are floating-point when the sample rate is not a reciprocal integer (for example, client_sample_rate 0.3 gives weight 3.333...). `toInt64` truncates toward zero, so estimated counts are systematically undercounted by up to one per bucket, and small/fractional accumulations can become zero. Use rounding or keep the result as a number/float instead of truncating.

findings.title: New aggregation relies on sample_weight but only sample_rate is populated
findings.body: This PR adds a SnQL aggregate `upsampled_count()` defined as `sum(sample_weight)`, but the only data-population change is in `src/sentry/testutils/factories.py`, which sets `normalized_data["sample_rate"]` from `client_sample_rate`. Nothing in the PR sets or ensures `sample_weight` exists on error events. If `sample_weight` isn't already stored or derived by Snuba ingestion for all allowlisted events, `sum(sample_weight)` will be null/zero and the endpoint will return 0 instead of the upsampled count. Verify the production ingestion path populates `sample_weight`, or compute the weight from `sample_rate` in the aggregate.
